```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
source(here::here("R", "A10", "A10_001-libraries.R"))
source(here::here("R", "A10", "A10_005-share_log.R"))
source(here::here("R", "A10", "A10_010-compare_shared_current.R"))

a10 <- readRDS(here::here("R_objects", "A10_010_comparison.rds"))

co  <- a10$cuts_old   # algorithm cut points
cn  <- a10$cuts_new   # alternative (grid optimum)
cal <- a10$calibration
gp  <- cal$grid_position
ss  <- a10$shared_steps
chg <- a10$changes

n_trans <- function(from, to) {
  x <- a10$transitions$n[a10$transitions$Change == paste(from, "to", to)]
  if (length(x) == 0) 0L else x
}
n_mech <- function(band, complaint, change) {
  x <- a10$mechanism$`Person-waves`[a10$mechanism$`T band` == band &
                                      a10$mechanism$`Self-rated memory` == complaint &
                                      a10$mechanism$Change == change]
  if (length(x) == 0) 0L else sum(x)
}

inputs_identical <- a10$rows$n_only_shared == 0 && a10$rows$n_only_current == 0 &&
  a10$inputs$tf_missing_mismatch == 0 && a10$inputs$tf_max_abs_diff < 1e-8 &&
  a10$inputs$d102_mismatch == 0 && a10$inputs$jorm_missing_mismatch == 0 &&
  isTRUE(a10$inputs$jorm_max_abs_diff < 1e-8)
reproduces <- inputs_identical && a10$rebuild$old_mismatch == 0 &&
  a10$rebuild$cur_mismatch == 0 && a10$rebuild$shared_vs_current == 0

pv <- a10$prevalence
pv_get <- function(y, k, what) pv[[what]][pv$year == y & pv$class == k]
ci_txt <- function(p, lo, hi) paste0(fmt_pct(p), "% (", fmt_pct(lo), " to ", fmt_pct(hi), ")")
pp_txt <- function(d, lo, hi) paste0(fmt_pct(d), " (", fmt_pct(lo), " to ", fmt_pct(hi), ")")
first_year <- min(pv$year)
n_other <- chg$n_changed - n_trans("Normal", "MCI") - n_trans("MCI", "Normal") - n_trans("MCI", "Dementia")
```

# Purpose

This report records the core algorithm classification file that was sent to Lindsay Kobayashi (LK) for the HRS-HCAP dementia incidence analysis, confirms that the current code reproduces it, and documents the procedure and the rationale for its cut points. It also describes an alternative pair of cut points that was considered in October 2026 and not adopted. Analysis A10 is the place to record later data shares (`R/A10/A10_005-share_log.R`).

# Summary

`r if (reproduces) paste0("The current code reproduces the file LK holds (", a10$files$shared, ") for all ", fmt_n(a10$rows$n_current), " person-waves: the inputs to classification (T score, self-rated memory, and IQCODE) are identical, and every class matches.") else "The current code does not reproduce the file LK holds for every person-wave; the checks below locate the differences."` The file stands, and no replacement will be sent.

The file classifies a person-wave with a T score below `r fmt_cut(co[["severe"]])` as severely impaired and below `r fmt_cut(co[["moderate"]])` as moderately impaired. These cut points were set in April 2026 so that the weighted Normal, MCI, and Dementia shares of the core algorithm in HRS-HCAP Wave 1 approximate those of the Manly-Jones algorithm (Manly et al., 2022): `r fmt_pct(cal$algorithm$share_normal)`%, `r fmt_pct(cal$algorithm$share_mci)`%, and `r fmt_pct(cal$algorithm$share_dementia)`%, against `r fmt_pct(cal$target_shares[["1"]])`%, `r fmt_pct(cal$target_shares[["2"]])`%, and `r fmt_pct(cal$target_shares[["3"]])`%. A grid search under the same criterion finds the closest pair at T < `r fmt_cut(cn[["severe"]])` and T < `r fmt_cut(cn[["moderate"]])`. That pair moves no share by more than `r fmt_pct(max(abs(c(cal$calibrated$share_normal - cal$algorithm$share_normal, cal$calibrated$share_mci - cal$algorithm$share_mci, cal$calibrated$share_dementia - cal$algorithm$share_dementia))))` percentage points and gives a 3-class kappa of `r fmt_k(cal$calibrated$kappa_3class)` against `r fmt_k(cal$algorithm$kappa_3class)` for the cut points in use, so it was not adopted.

# What was shared

```{r}
#| label: tbl-share-log
a10_share_log %>%
  mutate(Notes = unname(a10_share_notes[date])) %>%
  select(Date = date, File = file, `Sent by` = sent_by, `Sent to` = sent_to,
         Status = status, `Local copy` = local_copy, Notes) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Classification files prepared for LK (email thread \"HRS Algorithmic Dx\").")
```

LK received 2 files. The first (2026-06-11) left person-waves without a class when self-rated memory (HRS item D102, memory compared with 2 years ago) was missing, because the algorithm had no rule for that case. RNJ asked for D102 to be imputed, following the single-imputation approach used in Manly et al. (2022), and DT sent the second file (2026-07-10) with D102 imputed. This report assumes the July file is the one used in the incidence analysis. The copy checked here (`Data/`, file date `r a10$files$shared_mtime`) was saved from that email; git holds neither file, because data files are excluded from the repository. A third file with different cut points was prepared on 2026-10-17 and withdrawn before it was sent.

# How the shared file assigns a class

A person-wave with a T score is classified from 2 cut points and self-rated memory. Call the severe cut point $\tau_1$ and the moderate cut point $\tau_2$. A T score below $\tau_1$ gives Dementia when memory is reported as worse and MCI otherwise; a T score from $\tau_1$ to below $\tau_2$ gives MCI when memory is reported as worse and Normal otherwise; and a T score at or above $\tau_2$ gives Normal whatever the memory report. A person-wave without a T score (most often a proxy interview) is classified from the informant IQCODE alone.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-procedure
tibble::tribble(
  ~Step, ~`Shared file and current code`, ~Source,
  "Rows", "HRS Core respondents interviewed 2016 to 2022, all ages", "A7_075",
  "Cognitive score", "8 Core cognitive items; factor model fitted to HRS 2016, item parameters fixed for 2016 to 2022", "A7_050",
  "T score", "Factor score adjusted for age, sex, race and ethnicity, and schooling; mean 50, SD 10 in the HRS-HCAP robust normative sample", "A7_052, A7_055",
  "Self-rated memory (D102)", "Singly imputed when missing", "A0_019",
  "D102 codes counted as reported worsening", "Worse, don't know, refused, not ascertained (3, 8, 9, -8)", "A7_060",
  "Severe cut point, tau1", paste0("T < ", fmt_cut(co[["severe"]])), "A7_070",
  "Moderate cut point, tau2", paste0("T < ", fmt_cut(co[["moderate"]])), "A7_070",
  "How the cut points were set", "Chosen in April 2026 to approximate the weighted Manly-Jones class shares in HRS-HCAP Wave 1", "A7_070; April report",
  "No T score", paste0("IQCODE ", a10$jorm_cuts[["severe"]], " or higher: Dementia; above ", formatC(a10$jorm_cuts[["mild"]], format = "f", digits = 1), ": MCI; otherwise Normal"), "A7_060",
  "Unclassified", "No T score and no IQCODE, or D102 missing when T is below tau2", "A7_060",
  "ADL and IADL items", "Not in the rule; predictors in the D102 imputation only", "A0_019"
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Steps in assigning a class.")
```

Activities of daily living (ADL) and instrumental activities of daily living (IADL) do not enter the rule. Functional items reach the classification only as predictors in the imputation of D102.

# Evidence that the current code reproduces the shared file

```{r}
#| label: tbl-checks
tibble::tribble(
  ~Check, ~Result,
  "Person-waves in the shared file only", fmt_n(a10$rows$n_only_shared),
  "Person-waves in the current classification only", fmt_n(a10$rows$n_only_current),
  "Largest absolute difference in T score", fmt_sci(a10$inputs$tf_max_abs_diff),
  "T score missing in one version only", fmt_n(a10$inputs$tf_missing_mismatch),
  "D102 differs", fmt_n(a10$inputs$d102_mismatch),
  "IQCODE missing in one version only", fmt_n(a10$inputs$jorm_missing_mismatch),
  "Largest absolute difference in IQCODE", fmt_sci(a10$inputs$jorm_max_abs_diff),
  "Classes that differ, shared file versus current code", fmt_n(a10$rebuild$shared_vs_current),
  paste0("Shared file rebuilt from its own inputs with T < ", fmt_cut(co[["severe"]]), " and T < ", fmt_cut(co[["moderate"]]), ": classes that differ"), fmt_n(a10$rebuild$old_mismatch),
  "Current classification rebuilt from the written rule: classes that differ", fmt_n(a10$rebuild$cur_mismatch),
  "Current rebuild file (Data/) versus the A7 object: classes that differ",
    if (isTRUE(a10$current_file$exists)) fmt_n(a10$current_file$mismatch) else "File not found"
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Identity and reconstruction checks, all person-waves.")
```

The checks fall in 2 groups. The first compares the inputs: both versions hold the same `r fmt_n(a10$rows$n_current)` person-waves, the T scores differ by no more than `r fmt_sci(a10$inputs$tf_max_abs_diff)` T units (rounding in how the numbers were written to the file), and D102 and the IQCODE match. The second applies the written rule (`R/A7_060-algorithm_functions.R`) to each version's own inputs. `r if (reproduces) "Every class matches, so the shared file can be rebuilt exactly from the current code." else "Not every class matches; the counts in @tbl-checks locate the differences."`

# Rationale for the cut points

The cut points `r fmt_cut(co[["severe"]])` and `r fmt_cut(co[["moderate"]])` first appear in the A7 code committed on 2026-04-17. No code in the repository derives them. The report rendered from that commit (`Reports/A7_000-Main_control_2026-04-17.html`) sets the weighted class shares of the core algorithm in HRS-HCAP Wave 1 beside those of the Manly-Jones algorithm, which is consistent with cut points chosen by inspection to approximate the Manly-Jones class shares. The core algorithm is an adaptation of the Manly-Jones algorithm to the HRS Core, for waves and respondents without an HCAP assessment, so matching its class shares in the participants who have both keeps population estimates from Core data comparable to estimates from HRS-HCAP data.

Two alternatives were examined in October 2026. The first, the rule used for the legacy A1 algorithm (cut the T score at the quantiles that match the shares of HRS-HCAP Wave 1 participants with 2 or more and with 1 or more impaired cognitive domains), was tested with a rule written before the results were seen (`R/A7_072-domain_quantile_check.R`). It gave cut points near 36 and 43.5 on both the current and the April T scores, so it does not account for 37 and 48. The second is a grid search over pairs of cut points (step `r cal$grid_step` T units, `r fmt_n(gp$n_pairs)` pairs, `R/A7_070-threshold_calibration.R`), with the memory and IQCODE rules held fixed, which finds the pair whose weighted (`r cal$weight`) shares come closest to the Manly-Jones shares (`r cal$target_variable`, n = `r fmt_n(cal$n_sample)`).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-calibration
tibble::tibble(
  Classification = c("Manly-Jones algorithm (target)",
                     paste0("Core, cut points in use (", fmt_cut(co[["severe"]]), ", ", fmt_cut(co[["moderate"]]), ")"),
                     paste0("Core, grid optimum (", fmt_cut(cn[["severe"]]), ", ", fmt_cut(cn[["moderate"]]), ")"),
                     paste0("Core, highest kappa in grid (", fmt_cut(cal$max_kappa$cut_severe), ", ", fmt_cut(cal$max_kappa$cut_moderate), ")")),
  `Normal, %`   = fmt_pct(c(cal$target_shares[["1"]], cal$algorithm$share_normal,   cal$calibrated$share_normal,   cal$max_kappa$share_normal)),
  `MCI, %`      = fmt_pct(c(cal$target_shares[["2"]], cal$algorithm$share_mci,      cal$calibrated$share_mci,      cal$max_kappa$share_mci)),
  `Dementia, %` = fmt_pct(c(cal$target_shares[["3"]], cal$algorithm$share_dementia, cal$calibrated$share_dementia, cal$max_kappa$share_dementia)),
  `Kappa, 3-class` = c("", fmt_k(cal$algorithm$kappa_3class), fmt_k(cal$calibrated$kappa_3class), fmt_k(cal$max_kappa$kappa_3class)),
  `Kappa, dementia` = c("", fmt_k(cal$algorithm$kappa_binary), fmt_k(cal$calibrated$kappa_binary), fmt_k(cal$max_kappa$kappa_binary))
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Weighted (", cal$weight, ") class shares in HRS-HCAP Wave 1 and agreement with the Manly-Jones algorithm. The 3-class kappa uses quadratic weights. All kappas are in-sample."))
```

The cut points in use rank `r gp$rank` of `r fmt_n(gp$n_pairs)` pairs on the grid. Their largest difference from a Manly-Jones share is `r fmt_pct(gp$max_abs_share_diff_algorithm)` percentage points, against `r fmt_pct(gp$max_abs_share_diff_calibrated)` at the grid optimum, and their agreement with the Manly-Jones algorithm is `r if (cal$algorithm$kappa_3class >= cal$calibrated$kappa_3class) "slightly higher" else "slightly lower"` (3-class kappa `r fmt_k(cal$algorithm$kappa_3class)` against `r fmt_k(cal$calibrated$kappa_3class)`). The grid optimum would change the classification of person-waves LK has already analyzed for a small gain in matching the class shares, so the cut points in use were kept (RNJ, 2026-10-19).

# The alternative that was not adopted

This section shows what the grid optimum (T < `r fmt_cut(cn[["severe"]])` and T < `r fmt_cut(cn[["moderate"]])`) would have changed, applied to the same inputs as the shared file.

`r fmt_n(chg$n_changed)` person-waves (`r fmt_pct(chg$pct_changed)`%) would change class: `r fmt_n(n_trans("Normal", "MCI"))` from Normal to MCI, `r fmt_n(n_trans("MCI", "Normal"))` from MCI to Normal, and `r fmt_n(n_trans("MCI", "Dementia"))` from MCI to Dementia. `r if (n_other == 0) "No person-wave would move between Normal and Dementia or from Dementia to MCI." else paste0(fmt_n(n_other), " person-waves would make other changes (see @tbl-crosstab).")`

```{r}
#| label: tbl-crosstab
a10$crosstab %>%
  rename(`Shared file (rows) by alternative (columns)` = Shared) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), fmt_n)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Person-waves by class in the shared file and under the alternative cut points, all ages, 2016 to 2022 (unweighted counts).")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-change-wave
changes_tab <- a10$changes$all %>%
  select(Year, `All, n` = `Person-waves`, `All, changed` = Changed, `All, %` = `% changed`) %>%
  left_join(a10$changes$age65 %>% select(Year, `Age 65+, n` = `Person-waves`,
                                         `Age 65+, changed` = Changed, `Age 65+, %` = `% changed`), by = "Year") %>%
  left_join(a10$changes$hcap %>% select(Year, `HRS-HCAP Wave 1, n` = `Person-waves`,
                                        `HRS-HCAP Wave 1, changed` = Changed, `HRS-HCAP Wave 1, %` = `% changed`), by = "Year") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric) & !Year, fmt_n))
knitr::kable(changes_tab, caption = "Person-waves that would change class under the alternative, by year and sample (unweighted).")
```

```{r}
#| label: mechanism-text
up_sev   <- cn[["severe"]]   > co[["severe"]]
dn_mod   <- cn[["moderate"]] < co[["moderate"]]
worse    <- "Reported worse memory"
notworse <- "No reported worsening"
mech_sev <- if (up_sev) {
  paste0("In the band ", a10$severe_band, ", a person-wave that is moderately impaired in the shared file would be severely impaired. With a memory complaint it would move from MCI to Dementia (",
         fmt_n(n_mech(a10$severe_band, worse, "MCI to Dementia")), " person-waves); without one, from Normal to MCI (",
         fmt_n(n_mech(a10$severe_band, notworse, "Normal to MCI")), ").")
} else paste0("In the band ", a10$severe_band, ", a person-wave that is severely impaired in the shared file would be moderately impaired.")
mech_mod <- if (dn_mod) {
  paste0("In the band ", a10$moderate_band, ", a person-wave that is moderately impaired in the shared file would be unimpaired. With a memory complaint it would move from MCI to Normal (",
         fmt_n(n_mech(a10$moderate_band, worse, "MCI to Normal")), "); without one it is Normal in both (",
         fmt_n(n_mech(a10$moderate_band, notworse, "No change, Normal")), "), because the memory report decides the class only below the moderate cut point.")
} else paste0("In the band ", a10$moderate_band, ", a person-wave that is unimpaired in the shared file would be moderately impaired.")
```

`r if (a10$n_changed_outside_bands == 0) "Every person-wave that would change has a T score in 1 of 2 bands, the ranges between the 2 pairs of cut points." else paste0(fmt_n(a10$n_changed_outside_bands), " person-waves that would change have a T score outside the 2 bands, which a change in cut points alone cannot produce.")` `r mech_sev` `r mech_mod`

```{r}
#| label: tbl-mechanism
a10$mechanism %>%
  arrange(`T band`, `Self-rated memory`, Change) %>%
  mutate(`Person-waves` = fmt_n(`Person-waves`)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Person-waves with a T score between the 2 pairs of cut points, by self-rated memory and change in class under the alternative (all ages, 2016 to 2022).")
```

```{r}

pv %>%
  transmute(Year = year, Class = class,
            `Shared file, % (95% CI)` = ci_txt(p_old, lo_old, hi_old),
            `Alternative, % (95% CI)` = ci_txt(p_new, lo_new, hi_new),
            `Difference, points (95% CI)` = pp_txt(d, lo_d, hi_d),
            `Shared file, weighted N (× 1,000)` = format_weighted_thousands(wn_old),
            `Alternative, weighted N (× 1,000)` = format_weighted_thousands(wn_new)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Survey-weighted prevalence of each class among HRS Core respondents 65 and older, by wave, in the shared file and under the alternative cut points. Weights are the wave respondent weights; 95% confidence intervals use the HRS strata and sampling error computation units (logit intervals for prevalence, linearized intervals for the difference, which is estimated within the same respondents).",
                               weighted_thousands_note))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-weight-excluded
a10$weight_excluded %>%
  mutate(across(-Year, fmt_n)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Classified person-waves 65 and older, and those excluded from the weighted estimates because the respondent weight is 0 or missing.")
```

Among respondents 65 and older in `r first_year`, weighted dementia prevalence is `r ci_txt(pv_get(first_year, "Dementia", "p_old"), pv_get(first_year, "Dementia", "lo_old"), pv_get(first_year, "Dementia", "hi_old"))` in the shared file and would be `r ci_txt(pv_get(first_year, "Dementia", "p_new"), pv_get(first_year, "Dementia", "lo_new"), pv_get(first_year, "Dementia", "hi_new"))` under the alternative. Respondents with a respondent weight of 0 or missing (in the HRS, most often nursing home residents) do not contribute to these estimates, although they carry a class in the file.

# Assignment steps worth noting

These steps belong to the shared file and the current code alike. They are listed because they decide how a class is assigned.

Self-rated memory is singly imputed with the R package mice (Analysis A0, `R/A0_019-impute_self_concerns.R`), separately for each wave, with 1 imputation (seed 2) and the package default method for a numeric variable, predictive mean matching. Predictive mean matching copies an observed value from a respondent with similar predicted values, so an imputed D102 can be any observed code, including don't know (8), refused (9), and not ascertained (-8), which the rule counts as reported worsening. The predictors are the demographic terms (xP1 to xP7 and their interactions, with the matching terms in later waves), the Core cognitive items, the 16 IQCODE items, HRS items D554 to D556, and 10 functional items from HRS section G (G014, G021, G023, G030, G040, G041, G044, G047, G050, G059), read in `R/A0_012-recode_iadl.R`. In `r first_year`, `r fmt_n(ss$d102_imputed_2016)` of `r fmt_n(ss$n_2016)` person-waves have an imputed D102; `r fmt_n(ss$d102_imputed_2016_complaint)` of these imputed values count as reported worsening, `r fmt_n(ss$d102_imputed_2016_dk_rf_na)` of them as don't know, refused, or not ascertained. (The raw D102 is kept for 2016 only, so the count of imputed values in later waves is not available.) After imputation, `r fmt_n(ss$d102_missing_after_imputation)` person-waves still have D102 missing.

Responses of don't know, refused, or not ascertained count as reported worsening for `r fmt_n(ss$d102_dk_rf_na)` person-waves with a T score. The file assigns a class to `r fmt_n(ss$n_under65_classified)` person-waves younger than 65, although the norms apply from age 65 (`r fmt_n(ss$n_age_missing)` person-waves have no age). `r fmt_n(ss$n_unclassified)` person-waves are unclassified: `r fmt_n(ss$n_unclassified_no_tf_no_jorm)` have neither a T score nor an IQCODE, and `r fmt_n(ss$n_unclassified_tf_no_d102)` have a T score below the moderate cut point with D102 missing.

# Files and code

The report is rebuilt with `Rscript Analysis10_Driver.R` after Analyses A0 and A7. It reads `Data/`r a10$files$shared`` (the file as delivered, kept outside git), `Data/`r a10$files$current`` (written by A7_075, optional), `R_objects/A7_075_hrs16_22_long.rds`, `R_objects/A7_070_threshold_calibration.rds`, `R_objects/A7_075_hrs16_hcap.rds`, and `R_objects/A7_005_hrs16_22_merged.rds`, and it writes `R_objects/A10_010_comparison.rds`. The share log is `R/A10/A10_005-share_log.R`; for a new share, add a row there.

# References

Manly, J. J., Jones, R. N., Langa, K. M., Ryan, L. H., Levine, D. A., McCammon, R., Heeringa, S. G., & Weir, D. (2022). Estimating the prevalence of dementia and mild cognitive impairment in the US: The 2016 Health and Retirement Study Harmonized Cognitive Assessment Protocol project. *JAMA Neurology, 79*(12), 1242–1249. https://doi.org/10.1001/jamaneurol.2022.3543
